$comment: Chapter 2 — The Silent River (intro). Commentary varies with chapter-1 flags.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Three weeks after the cyclone, the rivers are still rising. The monsoon has parked itself over the delta like a guest who will not leave.

nodes.speaker: sharmin
nodes.text: "Tomorrow, definitely." That is what you told Alam. The newspapers quoted it. I am holding you to every word.

nodes.speaker: sharmin
nodes.text: Alam told the minister you would be honest about timelines. He respects that. So do I. Here is the honest number.

nodes.speaker: tanvir
nodes.text: Satellite pictures of the delta have stopped. Cloud cover nine out of ten. The river is rising in the dark.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: Not entirely dark. Radar sees through cloud — it paints the ground with its own light. The big agencies fly SAR exactly for this. VERIFY: NASA-ISRO NISAR.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: And we have the catalog now: a 27-unit bus, real panels, the hungry radar. Design her well. She will be heavier than anything we have flown.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Rain writes on the window in an alphabet nobody can read. Somewhere downriver, a union leader charges a lantern.

nodes.speaker: kabir
nodes.text: The river will not wait. To the design room.
